chapter: Arranging craft, ownership and the business
title: Intellectual property in the digital age
summary: Digital distribution has made rights and infringement complicated; he mentions a colleague's CD condemning streaming companies.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: I wanted to follow-up on something you just touched on about ownership. And you’ve done a lot of work in the field of intellectual property. Does the field and the guidelines and the way things work keep getting more complicated?

Extremely complicated. Yes. One of the whole digital rights movement and the very quick changeover to the distribution model of music now is very complicated. There’s just been a big reorganization of the mechanical rights organizations forming a consortium with the government’s permission. Things are changing very very quickly because you no longer have the physical control of the product. Record companies have no control. Individuals have no control. So it’s getting more and more difficult to identify what is an infringement. When it was a CD or an LP or a cassette or a video or whatever, there are certain licenses and certain revenue streams that you could follow. Now I know guys that are getting royalty checks for ten cents for two million plays on Spotify, or something like that — that’s an exaggeration, but these corporations have taken over and they’ve belittled the quality and the importance of music to everybody, so now it’s the climb back to fight back to say music is important and you should not minimalize its importance. Yeah, there’s some — I think Maria Schneider’s last CD was a finger point at all of the digital lords out there. I don’t know if you’ve heard it. It’s called “The Digital Lords.” It’s two CDs or something like that. But she’s pointing fingers at these large corporations that are, you know, living on the backs of creative artists.
You said, oh she finger pointed at them. Is that what you said?

Yeah, it’s called— what’s the name of the CD — she’s got two CDs and one is about the — well I don’t want to put words in her mouth, but basically she is condemning the digital lords who are out there, like the Spotifys and all that. And I’m sure there’s articles — I haven’t seen any but I’m sure she’s got some articles explaining that — I’ve got the CD in the other room I’ve played it on my radio show, but it’s a very intense piece of music, the whole package. It’s very intense.
